//: Run with `npm run mutate`. This list IS the ratchet: every glob in it has been paid down to 100% and `break: 100` below keeps it there. The Mutation workflow reads this array and runs one CI shard per entry, so adding a glob here is what puts a module under the gate — there is no second copy to update.
//testRunner: The vitest runner, which needs `assetsInclude: ["**/*.bin"]` in vitest.config.ts — without it stryker's own vitest instance cannot parse the binary photo fixture. It keeps the process warm between mutants and reports per-test coverage, so it is ~7x faster than the `command` runner (8m42s vs an hour for src/lib) and cannot produce the command runner's false 0.00 on a file its command failed to cover.
//coverageAnalysis: Set explicitly for runtime, not for correctness. `perTest` is what lets stryker run only the tests that cover a mutant — 2.6 to 7 per mutant across the ratcheted scopes — where `all` makes every mutant re-run the whole suite, which is what a static mutant already does and why src/lib (43% static) takes 30 minutes and modules/feed (0%) takes 4. It is NOT what makes CI's --incremental sound; that is `testRunner`, measured: the vitest runner populates coveredBy under perTest, all and off alike, while the command runner writes none and reuses every stored verdict including Survived. test/architecture/mutation-config.test.ts pins both and says which carries which argument.
//thresholds: break at 100 because src/lib is at 100. This is the ratchet: `npm run mutate` exits non-zero the moment a change drops it, so the debt cannot grow back quietly. If a genuinely equivalent mutant appears, prove it at the site with a Stryker directive and a sanctioned grant — do not lower this number.
//concurrency: 4, and it must not drift down again: it is this machine's performance-core count AND the vCPU count of a GitHub public-repo runner, so one number serves both and CI needs no override. It was dropped to 2 once (d0f2373, which reached main in #73) on the theory that the `browser` vitest project made a worker too heavy — a Chromium per worker on top of a workerd pool per worker — after 4 twice exhausted a 16 GB laptop that was also carrying three other worktrees. Measured 2026-09-19 on the machine that actually runs it (M4, 4P+6E, 24 GB) against `src/modules/products`: c=2 144s / 5.0 GB peak, c=4 107s / 6.9 GB, c=8 96s / 7.2 GB — and swap did not move on any of the three. Memory is not the constraint, and the drop cost ~1.7x on the mutant phase for nothing. What does NOT scale is the dry run: ~50s at every setting, because stryker forces `maxWorkers: 1` and runs the whole suite serially in one thread. Past 4 the workers land on efficiency cores at roughly a third the throughput, which is why 4->8 buys only 1.25x. The pressure that prompted the drop was real but was never THIS number: it is the NUMBER OF CONCURRENT RUNS — eight worktrees, each with an agent that can push — and a per-process cap cannot bound that. The machine-wide lock in `.githooks/pre-push` does; see the comment there.
//dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Raised from the default 5. The dry run is a full pass of the suite before a single mutant is tested, and it measures 1m31s to 2m19s on a quiet machine — 1244 tests, of which the striking part is the split: ~26s of actual test time against ~65s of harness overhead, because stryker forces `maxWorkers: 1` and runs the whole suite serially in one thread. Five minutes looks like 2-3x headroom and is not, because this is a laptop shared with three other worktrees: measured twice on PR #73, a concurrent suite in another worktree pushed it past the ceiling and the push failed after an hour with `Something went wrong in the initial test run` — a message that names neither the timeout nor a test, and sends you looking for a broken mutant that does not exist. Fifteen costs nothing when a run succeeds, because it is a ceiling and not a budget; all it changes is how long a genuinely wedged dry run waits before saying so. The companion fix is `testTimeout: 20_000` in vitest.config.ts, which handles starvation of an individual test; this handles starvation of the run.
//incremental: NOT set here, deliberately. `.github/workflows/mutation.yml` passes `--incremental` on the command line for each shard, where it is sound: a shard's `--mutate` is one fixed glob from the ratchet, so the stored report and the run always describe the same set. The commit gate's `--mutate` is a different set of changed files every run, and that workflow's own comment says `--incremental` is "safe here in a way it is not on the commit gate" — but setting it in this file turned it on for the gate and for every local `npx stryker run` as well, which is the one place it must not be. Measured cost of the contradiction: a mutant reported Survived that a test demonstrably killed (applying it by hand failed the test; a cold run scored 100). Chasing it cost an hour and the fix it invites — write another assertion — would have added a test nobody believed in. If a local survivor looks wrong, it now is wrong for some other reason.
//functions.ts: Each `!.../functions.ts` negation is the same fact: a server-function module imports `createServerFn`, which drags TanStack Start's virtual entries in with it, so it cannot be imported in the workers pool and cannot be mutation tested at all (D-41). The exclusion is only honest while those files hold nothing worth an assertion, which `test/architecture/server-functions-are-glue.test.ts` enforces.
//ignorePatterns: The eval's page cache is 22 fetched product pages at about 1.5 MB each, gitignored and never shipped. Stryker copies the project into a sandbox per run, so without this it copies 33 MB of marketing HTML every time and then tries to parse it — `DisableTypeChecksPreprocessor` reads a `.html` file as source and fills the log with BABEL_PARSE_ERROR from a shop's inline script. Harmless to the score and pure waste otherwise. Same reason `.stryker-tmp/` is in the eslint ignore list.
//lib: src/lib is three entries, not one glob, and positive paths rather than negations. It was the longest shard in every run — 31.8 minutes cold and 4.3 warm, about 2.5x the next one either way — because everything imports it and 43% of its mutants are static, and a static mutant re-runs the whole suite. contracts.ts and thermal.ts are 248 of its 367 mutants between them, so each gets its own shard. NEGATIONS WOULD BE WRONG HERE: the commit-gate analyzer appends every ! in this array to its own --mutate, so !src/lib/contracts.ts would exempt that file from the gate entirely. The cost of listing the rest positively is that a new file in src/lib would join no shard silently — which is why test/architecture/mutation-config.test.ts asserts the three entries cover the directory.
//e2e: Three Playwright support files, negated for the same reason as the schema ones below and with the same caveat: no positive glob has ever covered e2e/, so nothing is opted out, and the analyzer mutates them only because a diff touched them. They cannot be tested by the thing that does the mutating — stryker runs vitest, and most of what is left in demo.ts runs INSIDE THE BROWSER, injected through page.addInitScript, so every mutant in it comes back alive no matter what anyone asserts. What is NOT negated is the part that could be tested: holdFor and captionRule moved to e2e/support/caption.ts, which is mutated normally and sits at 100%. That split is the point — a whole-file exemption would have taken the caption's escaping rule with it, and that rule is what stops a narrated assertion being satisfied by its own narration. Exact paths, never a glob, so a new testable file under e2e/support is not swept in. Owner's call, 2026-09-12.
//db: The three schema files are negated for the one reason the `//lib` note says a negation is dangerous: it exempts a file from the commit-gate analyzer entirely. That IS the intent here, and it costs nothing, because no positive glob in this array has ever covered src/db — there is no coverage to lose, only an analyzer that mutates whatever a diff touches. Adding /*#__PURE__*/ to 23 sqliteTable() calls for the client-bundle fix (D-50) was enough to pull ~200 mutants of column names and index definitions into a push, in files the schema protocol makes a forbidden zone and that nobody may hand-edit to satisfy. Asserting a drizzle column name is not a test anyone should write — .fallowrc.jsonc already classes schema definitions with generated files and data tables for the same reason. Exact paths, never a glob, so a genuinely testable file added under src/db later is not swept in silently; and test/architecture/server-functions-are-glue.test.ts checks that each of these really is outside every positive glob, so the day one of them joins the ratchet this negation starts failing instead of quietly hollowing it out. Owner's call, 2026-09-12.
//routes: Every file under src/routes is negated, and the negations ride on the modules-components entry because they have no positive glob of their own — a negation-only entry makes stryker exit non-zero, so it could not be a CI shard. The commit-gate analyzer reads negations from the whole array, which is what keeps a route edit from being blocked by mutants no test can reach. What keeps the exclusion honest is test/architecture/server-functions-are-glue, which requires every route to hold nothing but imports, wiring and delegation.
